Delineate

/dih-LIN-ee-ayt/ - the stress falls on LIN · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Delineate means to describe or set out something in precise detail.

The pastry syllabus delineates each skill to be mastered, week by week, down to the fold count for a proper croissant.

Worked Example

Aunt Silve's will runs nine pages and reads like a land survey. It names which cousin takes the orchard rows east of the ditch, who gets the beehives and who the extractor, what happens to the tractor if two heirs want it, and the order in which the paintings choose their owners. The lawyer had warned her that loose wording breeds feuds; ten years on, the cousins still gather for the harvest, and nobody has ever gone to court.

Delineate is the exact word for what that will does, because it means to describe or set out something in precise detail — to draw the lines so plainly that nothing is left to argue about. Describe would cover a loose sketch; delineate promises edges.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

itemize: list piece by piece — delineate also draws how the pieces meet

map out: the planning phrase; delineate is its buttoned-up cousin

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

blur: smear the edges

gloss over: skip the details on purpose

Where it sits · how much detail the account gives — mention → describe → delineate

mention vs. delineate: Mention is a wave of the hand — the subject comes up and moves along.

describe vs. delineate: Describe goes further than mention — shape and color arrive; delineate claims the most: every line drawn, every edge exact, nothing left to guess.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: completely

Root — line-

Root — line-: line (Latin linea)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: to make, to do

Put it together

Put it together: De- (completely) + line + -ate = to draw the lines completely. Latin delineare was a draftsman's verb — to trace a design line by line — and the modern word keeps the drafting table in view: to delineate duties or borders is to draw them so exactly that everyone sees where one thing stops and the next begins. Here de- is not undoing anything; it is the intensifier, "all the way."

Use the root in a new word: linear

Use the root in a new word: linear: A linear plot moves like a drawn line — one event after another, no loops, no skips.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / precise

Delineate is for briefings and paperwork that must survive argument: duties, boundaries, ground rules. When plain telling will do, describe; when you only need the gist, sketch. It shares this unit's de- but not its direction — the prefix here means "thoroughly," so the word climbs where its neighbors pull down.
